function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

I don’t have a way to probe your connection from here, so I can’t tell you the exact numbers right now. But you can quickly find out your current download/upload speeds yourself with one of the following methods: | Method | How to run it | What you’ll see | |--------|---------------|-----------------| | **Web speed‑test** | Open a browser and go to (or ) | A quick test that shows download speed, upload speed, and ping. | | **Command‑line (Windows)** | 1. Open PowerShell or Command Prompt.
2. If you have `speedtest-cli` installed, run:
`speedtest` | Text output with download, upload, and ping. | | **Command‑line (Linux/macOS)** | 1. Install `speedtest-cli` if not already:
`sudo apt-get install speedtest-cli` (Debian/Ubuntu) or
`brew install speedtest-cli` (macOS).
2. Run:
`speedtest` | Same text output as above. | | **Mobile app** | Download the official Speedtest app from Google Play or the App Store. | Same metrics, plus a graph of the test. | ### Quick steps for Windows users If you want to run a test from the command line and you don’t have `speedtest-cli`, you can install it via Python’s package manager: ```powershell # Install pip if you don’t have it python -m ensurepip --upgrade # Install speedtest-cli pip install speedtest-cli # Run the test speedtest ``` If you prefer a one‑liner without installing anything, you can use the online test in your browser—just open and click “Go”. --- **What the numbers mean** | Metric | Typical values (home broadband) | What it tells you | |--------|---------------------------------|-------------------| | **Download speed** | 10 – 100 Mbps (or higher for fiber) | How fast you can pull data (e.g., streaming, downloads). | | **Upload speed** | 1 – 20 Mbps | How fast you can push data (e.g., video calls, uploads). | | **Ping / latency** | < 50 ms | How responsive the connection feels (important for gaming, VoIP). | If you run a test and share the results, I can help you interpret them or troubleshoot any issues. Happy testing!
